content.title: Maintaining Overall Focus and Paragraph Unity
content.overview: Effective ACT Writing requires every paragraph to serve a single controlling idea that directly supports the essay's central thesis. This lesson teaches the Anchor-and-Shift strategy to identify and remove distracting details while ensuring every sentence contributes to the overall argument.
learning_objectives: Identify sentences that stray from the paragraph's main idea or the essay's thesis.
Apply the Anchor-and-Shift strategy to restore paragraph unity.
Construct effective opening and closing sentences that link paragraph content to the central claim.

sections.title: The Principles of Unity and Focus
sections.content: Paragraph unity means that every sentence in a paragraph develops one single controlling idea. Overall focus means that this controlling idea explicitly advances the essay's thesis. In the ACT Writing section, a meandering paragraph weakens your argument. To maintain focus, you must ensure that the purpose of each paragraph is clear and that no 'rogue' sentences introduce unrelated anecdotes or isolated facts that do not support your specific point.

sections.title: The Anchor-and-Shift Strategy
sections.content: When a paragraph feels disorganized or includes unrelated details, use the three-step Anchor-and-Shift method: 1. Anchor: Start the paragraph with a clear sentence stating how this specific point ties to your thesis. 2. Prune: Review every middle sentence. If a sentence does not support the anchor, delete it or move it to a more appropriate paragraph. 3. Shift: End the paragraph with a closing line that transitions the specific evidence back to the essay's broader claim.

sections.title: The Final Check for Unity
sections.content: To verify paragraph unity, perform a 'Frame Check.' Read only the first sentence (the anchor) and the last sentence (the shift). Then, look at the middle sentences. If any middle sentence does not directly explain, prove, or illustrate the relationship between those two framing sentences, it is a distraction and should be removed.

worked_examples.question: Evaluate and improve this draft paragraph for an essay arguing that public parks deserve more funding: 'Parks are pleasant places to walk. Last summer the city repaved a bike path. Dogs run free there. Many cities also plant trees. Trees improve air quality. Volunteers sometimes clean up litter, but the city budget is tight.'
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Anchor. Create a topic sentence that links to the thesis: 'Public parks support community health by providing safe recreation and cleaner air.' Step 2: Prune. Remove 'Last summer the city repaved a bike path' because it is an isolated event that doesn't support the general health claim. Keep the sentences about trees and air quality. Step 3: Shift. Add a closing link: 'Because parks provide these essential health benefits, increased funding is necessary to maintain their infrastructure and environmental impact.' Result: A unified paragraph where every sentence supports the health-and-funding connection.

common_mistakes: Including 'interesting' facts that do not actually support the thesis.
Assuming a concluding sentence can fix a paragraph filled with unrelated details.
Failing to explicitly state the connection between a paragraph's evidence and the essay's main argument.
exam_tips: Every paragraph should have a 'job'—if you can't summarize that job in one sentence, the paragraph lacks focus.
Use precise transitions in your 'Shift' sentences to show the logical progression of your argument.
If you find yourself writing 'By the way' or 'Also,' check if you are introducing a distracting detail that should be pruned.
content.recap: To maintain focus and unity, every paragraph must be anchored to the thesis, pruned of distracting details, and shifted back to the central claim through a purposeful concluding sentence.

knowledge_claims.content: Paragraph unity is the principle that every sentence within a paragraph must develop a single controlling idea.
Overall focus in ACT Writing requires that every paragraph's controlling idea explicitly advances the essay's central thesis.
The 'Anchor' step involves stating how a paragraph ties to the thesis in one clear opening sentence.
The 'Prune' step requires removing or relocating any sentence that does not support the paragraph's anchor sentence.
The 'Shift' step involves adding a concluding line that links the paragraph's specific content back to the essay's overall claim.
The 'Frame Check' for unity involves ensuring the first and last sentences of a paragraph frame and support every middle sentence.
It is a mistake to assume that adding a strong concluding sentence can correct a paragraph that contains unrelated or distracting details.
A sentence that describes an isolated event or anecdote without connecting it to the main argument is a sign of drifting focus.
Opening and closing lines of a paragraph should orient the reader to the essay's argument and the logical progression of ideas.
When revising for focus, keep only the sentences that provide direct support for the paragraph's specific link to the thesis.
A paragraph lacks focus if its 'job' or purpose cannot be summarized in a single sentence tied to the thesis.
Unlike sentence-level cohesion, paragraph unity focuses on the logical relationship between all sentences and one central idea.

items.stem:
ACT WRITING PRACTICE: Repairable Products and Low Prices

Manufacturers can make products easier to repair, but doing so may raise initial prices.

Perspective 1: Institutions should adopt the option that produces the greatest measurable efficiency and access.
Perspective 2: Decisions should protect human relationships, local character, and individual judgment even when doing so is less efficient.
Perspective 3: A flexible policy with transparent safeguards can combine the strongest features of both approaches.

Write a unified, coherent essay in which you evaluate multiple perspectives on the issue and develop your own perspective. Explain the relationship between your perspective and at least one other perspective. Support your ideas with reasoning and examples.
items.correctAnswer: Scored holistically with the four ACT Writing domains
items.explanation: A strong response states a defensible position, engages at least one supplied perspective, develops reasoning and examples, organizes ideas coherently, and controls language and conventions.
